cands.bio: Republican member of the Alabama House of Representatives for District 7 since November 2022. Electrical engineering graduate of the University of Alabama in Huntsville. Worked ten years at Nucor Steel in Decatur and is now self-employed. He defeated incumbent Proncey Robertson in the 2022 Republican primary.
cands.gaps: We could not find where Ernie Yarbrough was born or when he came to Alabama, only that he was raised in Lawrence County. The pages read did not show any bills he sponsored, since Ballotpedia's sponsored-legislation table was empty. They also did not show any documented actions in office or stated positions on data centers, homestead property taxes, land ownership, growth and development, immigration, policing, guns, abortion, or school choice and teacher pay. His campaign site has topic headings such as 2nd Amendment, Lower Taxes, Pro-Life and Education, but the text of those pages was not available, so we did not record any positions from them. We found no news reports of controversies, no foreign ties and no endorsements; Ballotpedia says it identified no endorsements for 2026. He did not complete Ballotpedia's candidate survey in 2022 or 2026.

cands.bio: Dermatologic surgeon. Ran as an independent for Alabama House District 7 in 2026. Ballotpedia also lists a 2014 run for the Alabama State Senate as a Democrat, and a withdrawn Republican filing in 2026. No elected office is documented.
cands.gaps: We found no information on where he was born or raised or when he came to Alabama. He did not complete Ballotpedia's 2026 candidate survey, so his 2026 positions are not on record there. We found no 2026 statements from him on data centers, property taxes, land ownership, growth, immigration, campaign money, policing, guns, abortion or schools. We found no endorsements, no data-center or development stances, and no reporting of controversies. His 2014 campaign themes were the only stated positions available. They are twelve years old and do not address the issues this guide tracks.
